[IBNKATHIR:107:6/r1] IBNKATHIR, d. 774 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's account of a valley in Hell that Hell seeks refuge from 400 times daily, prepared for show-offs including Qur'an reciters, givers, pilgrims, and those who go out in God's path.
[IBNKATHIR:107:6/r2] IBNKATHIR, d. 774 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet says that whoever publicizes deeds for people will have God publicize him among creation and humiliate him; Ahmad gives another route through an unnamed man.
[IBNKATHIR:107:6/r3] IBNKATHIR, d. 774 · ابن المبارك | reports | Ibn al-Mubarak remarks, after the Abu Hurayra report about public notice, that it is a good hadith for show-offs.
[IBNKATHIR:107:6/r4] IBNKATHIR, d. 774 · author | holds | An act done for God does not become ostentation merely because people see it and the doer feels pleased by that.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r10] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The example is the late Asr prayer, performed without calm or reverence and perhaps only for show, like the hypocrites described elsewhere. | mentions 4, :, 1, 4, 2

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Doing a deed for God and then feeling pleased when people see it does not count as ostentation, as a report promises reward for both secrecy and publicity.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In a report Ibn Kathir calls strange through this chain, a man pleased that someone saw his prayer is told he has two rewards, for private and public worship.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p494/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن المبارك | reports | Ibn al-Mubarak is quoted as calling the report a good hadith for people who ostentatiously perform deeds.
[BURHAN:v1p202#2/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · مقاتل بن سليمان | reports | Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Surat al-Maun is Meccan except from فويل للمصلين through its end, which is Medinan.
[BIQAI:107:6/r1] BIQAI, d. 885 · author | holds | Their heedlessness means abandoning prayer materially when alone and corrupting it inwardly when gathered with others.
[BIQAI:107:6/r2] BIQAI, d. 885 · author | holds | They display prayer and other good deeds so people will see them, praise them, and do them favors, rather than seeking reward or fearing God's punishment.
[BIQAI:107:6/r3] BIQAI, d. 885 · author | holds | Because they seek only present people's approval, they leave prayer when no one is watching.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو جعفر بن الزبير | reports | He notes that people affiliated with Islam may push an orphan from his rights or fail to care for him, discourage feeding the poor, neglect prayer, show off, and withhold zakat or necessities.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو جعفر بن الزبير | reports | He reads these traits as those of a denier who expects no judgment, while observing that such acts can occur among Muslims without every person who commits them necessarily being a denier.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The author compares this trait-based description to hadiths that call one with four specified traits a pure hypocrite and say a fornicator is not a believer while committing the act.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostenta

tion and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their neglect means abandoning prayer privately and corrupting its inward quality in public; ostentation makes them perform deeds to win praise or kindness, not hope for reward or fear of God's punishment, so they leave prayer when unseen.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | These people may do lesser good ostentatiously but are so dominated by greed that they cannot even show off by giving a trivial benefit; the best people in God's sight benefit His dependents most.

[BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah has twenty-five words; counting from the beginning of prophethood points to year twelve AH, when Abu Bakr had eliminated the apostates and zakat-refusers, exposing their earlier prayer and almsgiving as mere show.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Abu Bakr's campaigns ended in that year with the defeat of Banu Hanifa at Yamama, people of al-Nujayr in Kindah, and al-Aswad al-Ansi in Sanaa.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The twenty-five words plus the four-word basmala point to year sixteen AH: Arab polytheists, Christians, and Magians had left the peninsula, most converting and the rest going to Byzantine lands.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The woe fell on showy worshippers who had been invited by their Prophet to pray but turned away, while other people followed them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p545/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Counting pronouns is unsuitable because the religion had become openly manifest and unobstructed; counting letters is also unnecessary after its public triumph became clear.

[BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r12] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The show-offs want people to see their worship so they will praise them; using seeing for praise is a general figurative expression or means recognition.

[BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r14] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Showing a voluntary act to encourage imitation is good; ostentation is acting so that eyes will see and praise, and avoiding it is exceptionally difficult.
[BURSEVI:v10p404/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The ostentatious person displays extra humility and signs of piety so onlookers will think him righteous; riya is seeking worldly benefit through worship, unlike hypocrisy, which conceals disbelief beneath visible faith.
[BURSEVI:v10p404/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | In the inward reading, one who attributes deeds and states to the dark ego is an ostentatious person.

[ALUSI:107:6/r1] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | They act when people can see them and let themselves be seen, seeking praise.

[ALUSI:107:7/r17] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91. | mentions 5:91
[ALUSI:107:7/r18] ALUSI, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some make the fāʾ causal from the preceding coordination, requiring the worshippers and deniers to be one group; they are then identified as hypocrites, a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Mālik, and supported by the ostentation clause.

[ALUSI:107:7/r24] ALUSI, d. 1270 · ابن إسحق والأشهب | reports | Ibn Isḥāq and al-Ashhab read yarāʾūna with a shortened form and a doubled hamza.

[ALUSI-FULL:v30p242#4/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They perform prayer when people can see them, seeking praise.

[ELMALILI:107:2-7#3/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Religious pretenders who neglect prayer, show off, and withhold even small help are more astonishingly blameworthy than disbelievers who deny religion and mistreat orphans and the poor.

[QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.

[QUTB-ZILAL:107:6/r2] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | The required act is establishing prayer, which requires conscious presence and standing before God alone.
